name: Cermait

attributes.attribute: avenged by his son Mac Cuill
a name also given to Ogma

text: Cermait means honey-mouthed in Irish. Writers also spell the name Cermat and Cearmaid. Two figures bear it. First, Cermait was a son of the Dagda. Lug Lamfhota killed him because Cermait had lain with Lug's wife. Cermait's son Mac Cuill later avenged him and speared Lug in return. Second, Ogma too bore this name. He serves as the god of poetry and of eloquence.

okr.objective: Cermait is an Irish byname borne by a son of the Dagda and by Ogma.
key_results: Lug Lamfhota killed Cermait over an affair with Lug's wife.
Mac Cuill avenged his father by spearing Lug.
Ogma, god of poetry, also bore the name.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
